description: Dependency stability in this repo comes from uv.lock plus `uv sync --frozen`
in CI -- hash-verified, reproducible installs that fail the build if the lock
and pyproject.toml drift. Renovate does not provide that stability; it only
delivers candidate updates. CI decides whether they land.
So updates are delivered silently. `automergeType: branch` means Renovate
pushes a branch, waits for the full CI suite (ruff, mypy, pytest, the
thresholded interpreter eval, and the OSV scan), and merges the commit to
main without opening a pull request. A PR is raised only when CI fails or
stays pending for 24h -- that is, only when a human is actually needed.
`security:minimumReleaseAgePypi` holds new PyPI releases for three days
before proposing them. Silent automerge removes the human eyeball from the
happy path, so that delay is what buys scanners time to catch a compromised
release before it reaches main.
schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

description: Vulnerability alerts skip the schedule and every concurrency limit, so a
fix is proposed as soon as it exists. `minimumReleaseAge: null` opts them
out of the three-day PyPI hold -- waiting out a quarantine window on a
known-exploitable CVE is the wrong trade.
This path reads GitHub's Dependabot alerts and requires the dependency
graph and Dependabot alerts to be enabled on the repo. `osvVulnerability-
Alerts` above is the independent channel: it queries OSV directly, needs
no GitHub setting, but covers *direct* dependencies only. A vulnerable
transitive package (e.g. starlette via fastapi) is reachable only through
the lockFileMaintenance refresh below.
Re-resolves uv.lock against current upstream without changing any
constraint in pyproject.toml. This is the only update type that can
remediate a transitive dependency, so it runs on its own weekly cadence
rather than waiting for the monthly batch.
One branch for every routine update, so the whole batch is gated by a
single CI run instead of one run per bump.
Majors carry the real breaking-change risk, so keep them out of the
batch and on their own branch. They still automerge on green -- the
point is blast radius: a failing major fails alone instead of blocking
every other update behind it. Flip `automerge` to false here if these
should be eyeballed instead.
Keep the lockfile refresh on its own branch too. Coupling the transitive-
CVE fix path to a routine version bump is how it ends up blocked behind
an unrelated failure.
